subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What gas is given off when a reactive metal reacts with a dilute acid?
questions.explain: Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen, so hydrogen gas is released.

questions.q: In a titration, which piece of apparatus delivers a precisely measured, fixed volume of one solution?
questions.explain: A pipette is used to measure an accurate fixed volume, while the burette delivers a variable volume.

questions.q: What colour does universal indicator turn in a strongly acidic solution?
questions.explain: Universal indicator turns red in strongly acidic conditions (low pH).

questions.q: When making a soluble salt from an insoluble base and acid, why is excess base added?
options: To ensure all the acid is neutralised
questions.explain: Excess insoluble base guarantees all the acid reacts; the leftover solid is then filtered off.

questions.q: What is the pH of a neutral solution such as pure water?
questions.explain: A neutral solution has a pH of exactly 7 on the 0–14 scale.

questions.q: Which acid is used to make a sulfate salt?
Two acids have the same concentration but acid X has a lower pH than acid Y. What can you conclude?
options: Acid Y is a stronger acid
Acid X is a stronger acid
questions.explain: At equal concentration, the acid that ionises more (lower pH) is the stronger acid.

questions.q: What are the products of a neutralisation reaction between an acid and a base?
questions.explain: Acid + base → salt + water is the general neutralisation reaction.

questions.q: A solution has a pH of 12. What does this tell you?
questions.explain: A pH greater than 7 indicates an alkaline (basic) solution.

questions.q: When a metal carbonate reacts with an acid, which gas is produced?
questions.explain: Acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.

questions.q: What is produced when an acid reacts with a metal oxide?
questions.explain: A metal oxide is a base, so acid + metal oxide → salt + water.

questions.q: Which salt is formed when hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide?
questions.explain: Hydrochloric acid produces chloride salts, so sodium chloride is formed.
